text:
Ancient cloisters on their broad walls

Unfold holy Truth in paintings,

Whose effect, warming pious entrails,

Tempers the coldness of their austerity.


In days when Christ's seeds were flowering,

More than one illustrious monk, now little cited,

Taking the cemetery for a workshop,

Glorified Death with simplicity.


—My soul is a tomb which, worst of cenobites,

From eternity I traverse and inhabit;

Nothing beautifies the walls of this hateful cloister.


Oh idle monk! When shall I know how to make

From the living spectacle of my sad misery

The work of my hands and the love of my eyes?

translation.title: The Bad Monk
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the soul-as-cloister conceit and the failure to turn misery into sacred art.
